full_judgment:
2. The facts, relevant for disposal of this petition, are that the petitioners herein as plaintiffs filed Other Class Suit No.16 of 2006 before the Assistant Judge, Dhunot, Bogra for permanent injunction in respect of the scheduled land described in the plaint stating, inter alia, that 14.12 acres land of C.S. Khatian No.32 of Mouza-Nimgasi was recorded in the names of Akbar Pramanik, Rafatullah Pramanik, Manikullah Pramanik, Isup Pramanik, Mishu Pramanik, Azimuddin Pramanik and Bahar Pramanik comprising 2 annas of share equally. Isup Pramanik executed a gift deed being No.1612 dated 13.04.1942 in favour of Mohammad Ali. Bahar Pramanik died leaving behind one daughter, Saton Bibi and two brothers named Mishu Pramanik and Azimuddin Pramanik. Saton Bibi sold her land in favour of Mishu Pramanik vide Registered Deed No.2265 dated 24.01.1952. Mishu Pramanik died leaving behind one wife named Diljan, three sons named Mohammad Ali, Pokra and Mir Boksh and two daughters named Jamela and Fatema. Azimuddin had no possession over the suit land except M.R.R. Khatian No.65, but M.R.R. Khatian No.49 was wrongly published in his name. Diljan died. Pokra Pramanik died leaving behind two sons and two daughters. Fatema died leaving behind husband-Nur Moahmmad, son-Fatik and daughter-Anisha. Nur Mohammad, Fatik and Anisha sold their portions of share in favour of plaintiff Nos.1-7. Mir Boksh died leaving behind plaintiff Nos.6 and 7. Mohammad Ali Pramanik died leaving behind second wife-Lilimon, three sons and three daughters. Lilimon died leaving behind two sons, i.e. plaintiff Nos.1 and 3 and two daughters. Subsequently, Azimuddin Pramanik died leaving behind three sons, i.e. defendant Nos.4 and 5 and Altaf and one daughter-Ayman. Altaf died leaving behind defendant Nos.1-3 and daughter-Aungura. Defendant No.5-Bhulu sold .03 acre land in favour of plaintiff No.4 vide Registered Deed No.3632 dated 01.07.1976. Subsequently, through another Registered Deed No.6490 dated 23.09.1990 sold .05 acre land in favour of plaintiff Nos.4 and 5 and others. Khatian Nos.221-223, 237, 459, 785 and 787 are published in the names of the co-sharers and on 05.03.2006, the defendants threatened the plaintiffs dispossession from the suit land; hence this suit. 

 3. The defendants contested the suit by filling written statements denyine all the material allegations in the plaint contending, inter alia, that C.S. Khatian No.32 was published in the mane of Azimuddin and others. Money Case No.2159 of 1942 was filed by the then Zaminder for arrear of rent before the third Munsif Court, Bogra against the C.S. recorded holder and obtained decree and filed Execution Case No.1143 of 1943. The said Zaminder auctioned the said land on 13.11.1943. Thereafter, Azimuddin Pramanik, Mishu Pramanik and Bahar Pramanik through settlement order took pattan from the Zaminder on 13.01.1951 and on the same date, other C.S. tenants through another settlement order took pattan from the Zaminder for the remaining part of the land. Accordingly, the gift deed being No.1612 dated 13.04.1942 was executed by Isup Pramanik is void. Bahar's daughter-Saton sold 54 decimals land in favour of Shahimuddin vide registered deed No.2262 dated 24.11.1952 and 48 decimals land in favour of Mishu Pramanik and M.R.R Khatian No.66 comprising 96 decimals land was published in the name of Azimuddin, M.R.R. Khatian No.49 comprising 405 acres land was published in the name of the heirs of Mishu Pramanik, M.R.R Khatian No.65 comprising 206 acres land was published in the name of Azimuddin. After the death of Azimuddin, his heirs opened separate Holding No.714 and enjoying the same and therefore, the suit is not maintainable. 

 8. Mr. SK. Mohammad Morshed, appearing for the petitioners, submits that the High Court Division committed error of law in affirming the judgment and order passed by the appellate Court below in rejecting the application under Order XXXIII, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure without considering that the plaintiffs have sufficient reasons to institute fresh suit for the same subject matter since both the parties are co-sharers under C.S. Khatian No.32, therefore, without demarcating or specifying the shares of the parties for permanent injunction is not tenable and as such, the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. He further submits that the High Court Division committed error of law in affirming the judgment and order passed by the appellate Court below in rejecting the application under Order XXXIII, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure and failed to consider that there is sufficient reason for bring a fresh suit for the same subject matter for proper relief and claim, therefore, the Court ought to have allowed the application for withdrawal of the suit by appreciating the provisions enshrined in Order XXXIII, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure and as such, the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. He further submits that the High Court Division committed error of law in affirming the judgment and order passed by the appellate Court below in rejecting the application under Order XXXIII, rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure and failed to appreciate that the said suit for permanent injunction filed by reasons of formal defect since the suit was against the co-sharers of a undivided and un-demarcated property and as such, the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside.
